Chania Cemetery at Etz Chayim Synagogue

Jewish Cemetery · Chania, Greece

Not demolished. Chania's Jewish community flourished under Ottoman rule from 1645, reaching a peak population before the Greek revolt of 1896 undermined its financial stability, driving many residents elsewhere; the community absorbed 200 refugees from Izmir in 1897 and 547 more Jews from the wider region seeking shelter during WWI. By 1941, only 314 Jews remained in Chania. In May 1944, 265 of the town's Jews were imprisoned for a week before being forced to board a ship; very few of those aboard are known to have survived, and those who did left Chania after the war, mostly for Israel and the United States.
